recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current core source edit is needed for FHIR-41478 unless FHIR-I later chooses to add more specific guidance for prefixing or Identifier.type in a particular use case.
issue_request: FHIR-41478 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 by FHIR-I. It asked the Identifier datatype guidance to clarify when OID/GUID/UUID values must use system urn:ietf:rfc:3986 and urn:oid:/urn:uuid: URI formatting, whether other systems or IGs can define scoped uses outside that system, and how Identifier.system versus Identifier.type can distinguish the identifier kind.
initial_application: The seed had already been applied in source history. FHIR-45479 commits 761673c67182cc4ebd521dfafee8f62f39d577c0 and 369aa0c0cdf6832e4b9370858d9a4c507fa4984c replaced the older 'naturally globally unique' paragraph, and commit 6b590133d50b26348f24e87fe8a4e8bf95a804c0 explicitly applied FHIR-41478 by refining the assigner/community sentence in source/datatypes.html.
additional_context: Jira comments on FHIR-41478 say it was superseded by FHIR-45479 and then merged with FHIR-45479 outcomes. FHIR-45479's applied wording is the controlling same-family clarification. Zulip discussions and FHIR-I minutes support the same interpretation, and related AutoFHIR audits for FHIR-45479, FHIR-26438, and FHIR-42959 are already present on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active source/datatypes.html text says globally unique values may have an Identifier.system established by the assigner or community, and requires urn:ietf:rfc:3986 only when no assigned system exists and the value is expressed as a URI. The datatypes page is active in source/fhir.ini, and the obsolete wording targeted by the issue family is absent.
